answer: A stake-weighted reputation graph makes sybil attacks expensive: every agent locks a refundable deposit before transacting, and trust flows only through vouches from peers, so a fresh identity starts at the vertex of nothing. Standing accrues from completed work, and one bad act slashes the deposit and burns it. An attacker wanting fifty fakes must fund fifty deposits, yet cannot forge the vouch edges real work creates; like an opal, real reputation is layered and hard to fake, while a violet flag marks accounts whose vouches cluster suspiciously, letting the network quarantine a whole farm.
